NAME: Payment Date Cleanup
DESC:
Payments are collected from several regional systems. Each system writes the payment date in its own format, and some systems send invalid or empty dates. The finance team needs a clean table with a real date column.

Implement solve so that it parses the payment dates, rejects invalid ones and returns the valid payments.

Input

payments_df

column type description
payment_id string unique, never null
customer_id string never null
amount string decimal text such as "25.50" or "40", never null
paid_on string payment date as free text; may be null

run_date is a string in the format yyyy-MM-dd.

Rules

  1. Leading and trailing spaces of paid_on are ignored.
  2. After trimming, paid_on is valid only if it matches one of these formats exactly and represents a real calendar date:
format example note
yyyy-MM-dd 2024-03-05
d/M/yyyy 5/3/2024, 05/03/2024 day first, then month; day and month have 1 or 2 digits
yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss 2024-03-05T14:30:00 only the date part is kept
yyyyMMdd 20240305

Any other format (for example 03-05-2024 or 2024-03-05 14:30:00), an impossible date (for example 2024-02-30), an empty string or null is invalid. 3. payment_date is the parsed date. A payment whose payment_date is after run_date is invalid. 4. Invalid payments are excluded from the output. 5. amount is converted to a double.

The Spark session of the grader uses spark.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy=CORRECTED: to_date returns null when a string does not match the given pattern.

Output

A DataFrame with exactly these columns, in this order:

column type
payment_id string
customer_id string
payment_date date
amount double

Rows are sorted by payment_date ascending, then payment_id ascending.

Example

run_date = "2024-03-31"

payments_df

payment_id customer_id amount paid_on
P1 C1 "100.00" "2024-03-05"
P2 C2 "25.50" " 5/3/2024 "
P3 C1 "40" "2024-03-04T23:59:59"
P4 C3 "10.00" "20240301"
P5 C2 "99.00" "2024-02-30"
P6 C3 "15.00" "03-05-2024"
P7 C1 "60.00" null
P8 C4 "70.00" "2024-04-02"

Expected output

payment_id customer_id payment_date amount
P4 C3 2024-03-01 10.0
P3 C1 2024-03-04 40.0
P1 C1 2024-03-05 100.0
P2 C2 2024-03-05 25.5

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(payments_df: DataFrame, run_date: str) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. Do not convert to pandas, do not call collect() or toPandas() inside solve, and do not use Python UDFs.
  • payments_df has up to 10^7 rows.
  • The returned DataFrame may be empty; its columns and types must still match the specification.

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# Variante robuste quelle que soit la configuration ANSI (Spark 3.5+ et 4.x) :
# try_to_timestamp renvoie null au lieu de lever une erreur quand le format ne correspond pas.
# (F.try_to_date n'existe qu'à partir de Spark 4.0.)
FORMATS = ["yyyy-MM-dd", "d/M/yyyy", "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss", "yyyyMMdd"]


def solve(payments_df: DataFrame, run_date: str) -> DataFrame:
    raw = F.trim(F.col("paid_on"))
    payment_date = F.coalesce(*[F.try_to_timestamp(raw, F.lit(f)).cast("date") for f in FORMATS])
    return (
        payments_df
        .withColumn("payment_date", payment_date)
        .filter(F.col("payment_date").isNotNull() & (F.col("payment_date") <= F.lit(run_date).cast("date")))
        .select("payment_id", "customer_id", "payment_date", F.col("amount").cast("double").alias("amount"))
        .orderBy("payment_date", "payment_id")
    )
